title: Unauthorized disclosure of parent account data during storage
description: Parent account personal data stored in MongoDB users collection may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or improper authentication mechanisms in the Authentication Service.
assumptions: Authentication Service has access to MongoDB users collection and stores parent account data
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as it represents explicit disclosure through the storage process

title: Data alteration of parent account information
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB users collection could be modified by unauthorized actors or through system vulnerabilities, leading to data integrity issues.
assumptions: MongoDB users collection is accessible and parent account data is sensitive
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 represents data alteration threat at the process level

title: Linkability of parent account data with other data sources
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB users collection could be linked with other datasets or user information, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across systems.
assumptions: MongoDB users collection may contain or be accessible to additional personal data
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 represents linkability threat at the datastore level

title: User Identifiability via JWT Token
description: The JWT token transmitted from the Authentication Service to the Parent User contains user data that can directly identify the user. This creates a privacy risk as the user's identity is exposed in the token payload.
assumptions: JWT token contains personally identifiable information (PII) in its payload

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Parent User
description: User data transmitted via JWT may be disclosed to unauthorized parties if the Parent User endpoint lacks proper authentication or if the JWT is intercepted during transmission. This violates data confidentiality principles.
assumptions: Parent User endpoint may not have adequate access controls

title: User Impersonation via JWT Token
description: If the JWT token is stolen or forged, an attacker could impersonate the authenticated user when communicating with the Parent User system, leading to unauthorized access and potential data manipulation.
assumptions: JWT token may be intercepted or compromised during transmission

title: JWT Token Tampering and Data Integrity Loss
description: The JWT token containing user data could be tampered with during transmission if proper cryptographic signing is not enforced, leading to data integrity violations and potential manipulation of user information.
assumptions: JWT may not be cryptographically signed or validated properly

title: Child Login Linked to Parent Identity
description: Child's login activity using parent email credentials can be linked to the parent's identity, potentially exposing the child's online behavior to the parent or third parties who can access parent account information.
assumptions: Parent email is identifiable and linked to parent identity

title: Child Identity Revealed Through Parent Credentials
description: The child's identity becomes identifiable through the parent email and password used during authentication, potentially exposing the child's relationship to the parent and their usage patterns.
assumptions: Parent email is publicly or semi-publicly associated with the child

title: Parent Credentials Disclosed During Transmission
description: Parent email and password transmitted during child login could be intercepted or logged, exposing sensitive authentication credentials and potentially enabling unauthorized access to parent accounts.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully encrypted or credentials are logged

title: Child Identity Usurped by Unauthorized Actor
description: An attacker could potentially usurp the child's identity by obtaining parent credentials, gaining unauthorized access to child-specific services or data.
assumptions: Parent credentials are compromised or intercepted

title: Linkability of Child Identity Across Systems
description: The JWT token and child profiles transmitted from the Authentication Service could be linked to identify the child user across different services or contexts, potentially enabling cross-service tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The JWT and profile data contain unique identifiers that can be correlated across systems.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node; specific child profile context may warrant more granular analysis.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Child Profile Data
description: Child profile information transmitted via the authentication flow could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or at the receiving endpoint, violating child privacy protections.
assumptions: The transmission channel or receiving endpoint may lack adequate access controls.
uncertainty_note: Severity elevated due to child data sensitivity; actual risk depends on encryption and endpoint security.

title: Authentication Token Misuse for Identity Usurpation
description: The JWT token could be intercepted or misused by unauthorized actors to impersonate the child user, gaining access to services or data under the child's identity.
assumptions: JWT tokens may be transmitted or stored insecurely, enabling token theft or replay attacks.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a general usurpation node; specific JWT token lifecycle details would refine this assessment.

title: Linking of child profile data with other records
description: The government ID (govt ID) collected during child profile creation can serve as a unique identifier that enables linking this profile data with other databases or records, potentially revealing additional information about the child or parent beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: The system or external parties have access to other databases containing the same government ID.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 from context [5] as it describes linking via recurring identifiers

title: Identification of child through profile data
description: The combination of name, DOB, gender, and government ID can uniquely identify the child, potentially exposing the child's identity to unauthorized parties or enabling profiling.
assumptions: The data is accessible to parties who should not have access to identify the child.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a standard identification threat node

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive child profile data
description: The Child Profile Management process may disclose sensitive data (especially government ID) to unauthorized internal or external parties during processing or storage.
assumptions: The process has inadequate access controls or data protection measures.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a standard disclosure threat node

title: Disclosure of child profile data to third parties
description: The process may share child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) with third parties (e.g., government agencies, service providers) without proper consent or legal basis.
assumptions: Third-party sharing occurs without adequate privacy safeguards or user consent.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a standard third-party disclosure threat node

title: Child Profile Data Identifiability Risk
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB contains personally identifiable information (PII) that can directly identify the child. The data may include names, dates of birth, contact information, and other sensitive details that make the child identifiable to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Child profile data contains sufficient PII to identify the child

title: Unauthorized Child Profile Data Disclosure
description: Child profile data may be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unintended data transfers. The explicit disclosure of child data to external systems or implicit disclosure through metadata could violate privacy expectations.
assumptions: Access controls may be insufficient or misconfigured

title: Child Profile Data Alteration Risk
description: Child profile data may be altered, corrupted, or deleted without proper authorization. The update functionality in the Child Profile Management process creates opportunities for unauthorized modifications to sensitive child information.
assumptions: Update mechanisms lack adequate access controls and audit trails

title: Child Profile Data Linkability Risk
description: Child profile data may be linked with other data sources (e.g., school records, healthcare data, parental information) creating a comprehensive profile that exceeds the minimality principle. This linking could enable re-identification or profiling of the child.
assumptions: Child profile data may be correlated with external data sources

title: Child Privacy Regulation Non-Compliance Risk
description: Storage and processing of child profile data may violate child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K, state child privacy laws). The data flow may not adequately address consent requirements, data minimization, or parental rights.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child data are stringent and must be followed

title: Linkability of video search patterns to user identity
description: Video search queries and patterns from the Child User (EE2) could be linked to their identity through metadata, timestamps, or associated comments, potentially revealing user interests and behavior patterns.
assumptions: System logs search queries with user identifiers or session data that can be correlated.

title: Identifiability through video content and comments
description: Video content uploaded or searched by the Child User (EE2), along with their comments, could contain personally identifiable information that identifies the user to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Video content or comments may contain metadata, location data, or other identifying information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content and comments
description: Video content and comments from the Child User (EE2) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Video Management Service (P2) may have inadequate access controls or data sharing policies.

title: Improper personal data management of video content and comments
description: Personal data (video content, comments) from the Child User (EE2) may be managed non-compliantly with privacy regulations, including retention, deletion, or processing issues.
assumptions: Data management practices may not fully comply with applicable privacy regulations.
uncertainty_note: Context [5] references Nc.2 for improper personal data management, which applies to this flow.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata (e.g., timestamps, locations, device IDs, user IDs) can contain or reveal identifying information about individuals captured in the videos.
assumptions: Metadata is stored alongside video files and may be indexed/searchable
uncertainty_note: Citation I.1.2 from context applies to metadata; video files themselves also contain identifying information

title: Unauthorized video data disclosure
description: Video files and metadata stored in MongoDB could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unintended sharing mechanisms.
assumptions: Video data contains personal information and is accessible beyond intended recipients
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard disclosure node; specific disclosure mechanisms not detailed in flow

title: Linkability of video data across contexts
description: Video content and metadata can be linked to identify individuals across different systems, time periods, or contexts, enabling profiling and tracking.
assumptions: Video data is persistent and potentially accessible across multiple systems or timeframes
uncertainty_note: L.1.1 is a standard linkability node; specific linking mechanisms depend on system architecture

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child search and watch history
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection stores sensitive child search and watch history data. If access controls are inadequate, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties, violating the minimality principle and exposing children's behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard MongoDB deployment without additional access controls specified

title: Linkability of child profile data across systems
description: Child search and watch history stored in DS2 could be linked with other data sources (e.g., parent accounts, device IDs) to create comprehensive profiles of the child, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral patterns and preferences.
uncertainty_note: Assuming potential for data linkage with other systems not explicitly modeled

title: Identifiability of child through search/watch history
description: The stored child search and watch history may contain personally identifiable information or unique behavioral patterns that could be used to identify the child, especially when combined with other data.
uncertainty_note: Assuming search/watch history may contain identifiable content

title: Unintended disclosure during child profile management
description: The Child Profile Management process may inadvertently disclose child search and watch history data during normal operations (e.g., logging, debugging, or error messages), leading to implicit data disclosure.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard process implementation without explicit disclosure controls

title: Usurpation of child profile management
description: An unauthorized actor could potentially manipulate the Child Profile Management process to access or modify child search and watch history, impersonating legitimate users or exploiting authentication weaknesses.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard authentication mechanisms may have vulnerabilities

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: The Child Profile Management process may fail to comply with GDPR-K or COPPA requirements regarding collection, storage, and processing of children's personal data, particularly concerning search and watch history.
uncertainty_note: Assuming regulatory requirements apply to this data flow

title: Video data linkability to user identity
description: Video upload data can be linked to the Parent User (EE1) across different sessions or contexts, potentially enabling tracking of user behavior patterns over time.
assumptions: Video metadata and timestamps are retained and associated with user account

title: Video content inherently identifies user
description: Video content inherently contains identifiable information about the Parent User, including biometric data, location, and behavioral patterns that can be used to identify the individual.
assumptions: Video content is processed and stored by the Video Management Service

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: Video data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during storage, processing, or transmission, potentially violating user privacy expectations.
assumptions: Video data is transmitted and stored in the Video Management Service

title: Improper personal data management in approval workflow
description: The approval/rejection process may involve improper personal data management, including inadequate retention policies, insufficient access controls, or non-compliance with data protection regulations during video data handling.
assumptions: Video data undergoes approval/rejection workflow with multiple access points
uncertainty_note: Context [5] mentions Nc.2 for improper personal data management, which applies to this approval workflow scenario

title: Video stream linkable to child identity
description: The video stream from the Video Management Service to the child user could be linked to the child's identity through metadata, timestamps, or contextual information, enabling correlation with other personal data.
assumptions: Video metadata or contextual data is available and accessible for linking purposes.

title: Video content reveals identifiable information
description: The video stream may contain visual or audio content that identifies the child or other individuals (e.g., family members, caregivers), creating privacy risks for all persons depicted.
assumptions: Video content is not sufficiently anonymized or blurred for sensitive individuals.

title: Video stream disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The video stream could be intercepted, recorded, or accessed by unauthorized third parties during transmission, leading to unauthorized disclosure of personal video content.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully secured or encryption is insufficient.

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Streaming video of a child may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding collection, processing, and transmission of children's personal data without proper consent or safeguards.
assumptions: Applicable regulations require explicit consent and specific safeguards for children's video data.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction; this is a general compliance concern.

title: Unintended disclosure of child browsing data to AI engine
description: Child browsing data from MongoDB collection is transferred to AI Recommendation Engine, potentially exposing sensitive personal data of minors to third-party AI service. This represents an explicit disclosure that may violate minimality principle and children's privacy protections.
assumptions: AI engine may share data with third parties or store it beyond intended scope
uncertainty_note: Citation Dd.1.1 from context is approximate for this specific child data scenario

title: Child browsing data may identify individual children
description: Browsing data from childprofiles collection contains patterns and behaviors that could be used to identify specific children, especially when combined with other data sources. This identifiability risk is heightened for minors.
assumptions: Browsing patterns are unique enough to identify individuals
uncertainty_note: Context I.1.1 is general identifiability node; specific child data context not fully covered

title: Non-compliance with children's data protection regulations
description: Transferring child browsing data to AI Recommendation Engine may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other children's privacy regulations requiring explicit consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation for minor data processing.
assumptions: AI engine processing may not have appropriate legal basis for child data
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is general non-compliance node; specific regulatory requirements for child-AI data flow not fully detailed in context

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: Browsing data is intentionally transferred from the AI Recommendation Engine to Third-Party Advertisers as part of the planned data flow. This represents an explicit disclosure by design, raising questions about data minimality and whether this sharing is strictly necessary for the system's purpose.
assumptions: Advertisers receive identifiable or quasi-identifiable browsing data that could be used for profiling or targeted advertising.

title: Linkability of Browsing Data with External Data Sources
description: Third-Party Advertisers may link the received browsing data with other data sources they possess (e.g., purchase history, social media profiles), creating comprehensive user profiles beyond what was originally intended.
assumptions: Advertisers have access to multiple data sources and can correlate browsing behavior with other personal information.

title: Identification of Users from Browsing Data
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers may contain or enable identification of individual users, potentially revealing personal habits, interests, or behaviors that could be used to identify specific individuals.
assumptions: Browsing patterns are unique enough to identify individuals, or can be combined with other data to achieve identification.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of government ID images during storage
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be accessed or disclosed to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, improper permissions, or security vulnerabilities in the authentication service or file system.
assumptions: The authentication service and file system have proper access controls and encryption in place.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for unauthorized data disclosure during storage based on LINDDUN Pro methodology.

title: Tampering with stored government ID images
description: Government ID images could be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during storage in the file system, compromising the integrity of the authentication data.
assumptions: The file system has integrity checks and access controls in place.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for data integrity threats during storage.

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: Unauthorized individuals or systems could access the stored government ID images through weak authentication, insufficient access controls, or security misconfigurations in the authentication service or file system.
assumptions: The authentication service implements proper authentication and authorization mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable threat-tree node for unauthorized access threats.

title: JWT Token Disclosure via XSS
description: JWT stored in browser localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, making it vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Malicious scripts can read and exfiltrate the token, leading to unauthorized disclosure of authentication credentials.
assumptions: Assumes the application is vulnerable to XSS or runs untrusted third-party scripts
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a standard disclosure node for data store vulnerabilities

title: Session Hijacking via Token Theft
description: JWT tokens stored in localStorage can be stolen by attackers (via XSS, network sniffing, or browser compromise) and used to impersonate the legitimate user, enabling session hijacking and unauthorized access to protected resources.
assumptions: Assumes JWT contains session claims and is used for authentication
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 is a standard usurpation node for token-based authentication

title: JWT Token Manipulation
description: Since localStorage is accessible to JavaScript, malicious scripts can modify the stored JWT token, potentially altering user roles, permissions, or session claims, leading to privilege escalation or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes JWT is not cryptographically signed or is signed with a weak key
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a standard data manipulation node for data store vulnerabilities

title: Linking of child history data to parent profile
description: The child history data retrieved for parent review may be linked with other data elements (e.g., parent's other children, medical records, or behavioral data) to build a comprehensive profile of the child or family, potentially revealing sensitive information beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Parent has access to other data sources that can be combined with this child history data
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 chosen based on general LINDDUN methodology for linking threats; exact node may vary by implementation

title: Over-disclosure of child history information
description: The child history data retrieved may contain more detailed or sensitive information than necessary for the parent's review, potentially exposing private details about the child's development, health, or behavior that should remain confidential.
assumptions: The system retrieves comprehensive child history without applying appropriate data minimization
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 chosen based on general LINDDUN methodology for disclosure threats; exact node may vary by implementation

title: Parent may not fully understand child history data implications
description: The parent reviewing child history may not fully comprehend the implications of the data they are viewing, including what information is being shared, how it might be used, or the long-term privacy consequences of this data access.
assumptions: Parent lacks technical literacy or privacy awareness regarding the data they are accessing
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.1 chosen based on general LINDDUN methodology for understanding threats; exact node may vary by implementation
